title: Dynamic Method Dispatch and Reflection
subtopics: Public and private method access considerations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of dynamic method dispatch and reflection in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply dynamic method dispatch and reflection in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to appropriate uses of reflection and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Dynamic Method Dispatch and Reflection through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding dynamic method dispatch and reflection helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Dynamic Method Dispatch and Reflection helps you reason about invoking methods dynamically. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Invoking methods dynamically. Then connect it to Inspecting object methods. The remaining syllabus points—Public and private method access considerations, Appropriate uses of reflection—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Dynamic Method Dispatch and Reflection
content_blocks.code:
class Greeter
  define_method(:hello) { "hello from Ruby" }
end
puts Greeter.new.public_send(:hello)

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports dynamic method dispatch and reflection. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for dynamic method dispatch and reflection using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Appropriate uses of reflection), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain dynamic method dispatch and reflection, identify its place in advanced language features and metaprogramming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
